issues.description: The SealSaloon class attribute 'orders' is specified differently across artifacts. Problem statement (and UML) requires a modifiable List<Meal> named orders (explicitly described in the tasks), but the reference solution declares orders as a Meal[] array (SealSaloon.java) and the template repository provides ArrayHelpers utilities that operate on arrays. This inconsistency leaves students unsure whether to implement orders as java.util.List<Meal> (matching the textual requirement/UML) or as a Meal[] (matching the template helpers and solution), and which APIs (List methods vs. ArrayHelpers) they should use.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the expected type for the 'orders' attribute consistent across the problem statement, UML, template, and solution. Two viable options: (A) Accept array-based implementation: update the problem statement and UML to specify 'Meal[] orders' (or an array-backed orders) and explicitly instruct students to use the provided ArrayHelpers methods; or (B) Adopt List<Meal>: update the template (add helpers or use java.util.List in the template), change the solution to use List<Meal>, and revise examples/UML to List. Ensure all examples and the UML text match the chosen representation so students are not forced to reconcile conflicting guidance.
